1	# Fleet Wiring — Handoff / Resume Notes
2	
3	Turning `lab-fleet` from published reference config into **GitOps that Rancher
4	Fleet deploys** to this cluster. Full plan (private): Cowork workspace
5	`_portfolio/ash4d-lab/fleet-wiring-plan.md`. This file is the short resume note
6	for picking the work back up.
7	
8	Verified against the live cluster **2026-07-29**.
9	
10	## Topology
11	
12	- **Rancher controller** — `v2.14.3` at `https://rancher.ash4d.com`
13	  (**192.168.7.148**, separate host). GitRepo/Bundle objects live here, and the
14	  local `kubectl` context named **`rancher`** already has API access to them —
15	  no Rancher API token needed (see Phase 0).
16	- **This cluster** — `sdf1`, downstream `c-nnzn9` at **192.168.7.149**.
17	  `fleet-agent v0.15.4`'s pod is Running, but it has **never registered** — see
18	  the blocker section below. Its only bundle is its own `fleet-agent-c-nnzn9`.
19	- Deploy source is **`lab-fleet` directly**, not `ash4d.com/lab` (Fleet doesn't
20	  init git submodules, so a GitRepo on `ash4d.com` would clone an empty gitlink).
21	  Public repo → no clone secret needed.
22	- Note the downstream cluster has **no Fleet CRDs** — that is normal for this
23	  Fleet version (`EXPERIMENTAL_COPY_RESOURCES_DOWNSTREAM=false`). Bundle state is
24	  read on the controller, not here. See Verify below.
25	
26	## ✅ Phase 1 — DONE (committed AND pushed to `main`)
27	
28	Every deployable numbered dir has a `fleet.yaml`:
29	
30	- **Helm bundles** (`takeOwnership: true`, versions pinned to the running
31	  releases so Fleet adopts instead of upgrading):
32	  metallb `0.16.1`, longhorn `1.12.0`, nvdp `0.19.2`, dcgm-exporter `4.8.2`,
33	  ollama `1.67.0`, open-webui `14.8.0`, milvus `5.0.22`. Chart versions all match
34	  the running releases. Two needed values corrections — see the log below;
35	  comparing `helm get values` alone was **not** sufficient to catch them.
36	- **Raw-manifest bundles:** comfyui, the three doc indexers, mcp, hermes, emby,
37	  node-red, resilio, plus metallb pools, the nvidia RuntimeClass, attu,
38	  ollama-exporter, and docs-rag. **Every one of these also sets
39	  `helm.takeOwnership: true`** — Fleet deploys raw manifests through Helm
40	  internally, and the pre-existing objects carry no `meta.helm.sh/release-name`
41	  annotation, so without it the first sync fails on ownership. With it, adoption
42	  is metadata-only: Helm labels land on the top-level objects, pod templates are
43	  untouched, and nothing restarts.
44	- Where a dir had a chart **and** raw manifests, the raw manifests were moved
45	  into a sibling subdir so each chart owns its own bundle path (Fleet = one
46	  chart per path): `01-networking/pools/`, `03-gpu/{dcgm-exporter,runtimeclass}/`,
47	  `06-milvus/attu/`, `04-ollama/ollama-exporter/`.
48	- Placeholder/unapplied manifests are renamed `.yaml.txt` so Fleet never applies
49	  them: `09-mcp/github-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt`,
50	  `10-hermes/hermes-webui.secret.example.yaml.txt`,
51	  `07-comfyui/comfyui-user-script.yaml.txt`.
52	- `00-host` and `14-cluster-mgmt` stay docs-only (no `fleet.yaml`). Traefik is
53	  k3s-bundled and not Fleet-managed (`traefik-values.yaml` is reference only).
54	
55	## ✅ Phase 0 — Enable CD on the controller: ALREADY DONE
56	
57	The earlier note here assumed the `fleet` feature was off and that a Rancher API
58	token was needed. Both were wrong as of 2026-07-29:
59	
60	- The `fleet` feature is **enabled** (`features.management.cattle.io/fleet`:
61	  `spec.value` unset, `status.default: true`). Nothing to PUT.
62	- `kubectl --context rancher` reaches the GitRepo/Bundle/BundleDeployment CRDs
63	  directly, so the whole flow can be driven with `kubectl` — no `RTOKEN`, no
64	  `/v3/features` call.
65	- `c-nnzn9` is registered in workspace **`fleet-default`**.
66	- At the start of this work there was a second GitRepo,
67	  `fleet-default/ash4d-site` → `https://github.com/darthzen/ash4d.com`,
68	  `paths: ["deploy"]`, target `site=ash4d`, which resolved to the junk
69	  `cluster-ee8f7993b3a6` rather than `c-nnzn9`. Both it and its bundle were gone
70	  later the same session (not removed as part of this work) and the junk cluster
71	  has since been deleted — see the cleanup note below. **`c-nnzn9` is now the only
72	  Fleet-managed downstream**, alongside `fleet-local/local`.
73	
74	**Target label for this cluster:** `c-nnzn9` already carries a bespoke
75	`ash4d-lab: ""` label — use that rather than
76	`management.cattle.io/cluster-name`, which is Rancher-managed. (The old
77	`site=ash4d` selector belonged to the deleted junk cluster; do not reuse it.)
78	
79	```yaml
80	targets:
81	  - clusterSelector:
82	      matchLabels:
83	        ash4d-lab: ""
84	```
85	
86	## ✅ RESOLVED — fleet-agent registration (was blocking everything)
87	
88	Found 2026-07-29 while applying the first GitRepo, **fixed the same day** with
89	Option A below. Symptom: bundles reached `WaitApplied` and sat there, with the
90	BundleDeployment getting no status at all, because the downstream agent never
91	picked it up.
92	
93	```
94	Failed to register agent: registration failed: cannot create clusterregistration
95	on management cluster ... tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: failed to load
96	system roots and no roots provided; open /dev/null: not a directory
97	```
98	
99	Diagnosis — it is a policy mismatch, not a network or image problem:
100	
101	| Check | Result |
102	|---|---|
103	| Agent → Rancher network | ✅ `wget https://rancher.ash4d.com/ping` returns `pong` |
104	| CA roots in the agent image | ✅ 435 certs in `/var/lib/ca-certificates/pem` |
105	| Rancher server cert | ✅ valid, public **Let's Encrypt** (`CN=YR1`, expires 2026-10-15) |
106	| `agent-tls-mode` (controller) | ⚠️ **`strict`** (Rancher default) |
107	| `apiServerCA` in `fleet-agent-bootstrap` | ❌ **empty, 0 bytes** |
108	
109	`strict` mode requires an explicitly-provided CA and will not fall back to system
110	roots. With `apiServerCA` empty, registration can never succeed — regardless of
111	the fact that the cert is publicly trusted.
112	
113	Two fixes:
114	
115	**A — switch to the system trust store** (matches a publicly-trusted Rancher cert,
116	and is Rancher's supported configuration for one):
117	
118	```bash
119	kubectl --context rancher patch settings.management.cattle.io agent-tls-mode   --type=merge -p '{"value":"system-store"}'
120	```
121	
122	Controller-wide: it affects **every** downstream agent, not just sdf1. Agents
123	redeploy their bootstrap config afterwards.
124	
125	**B — populate `apiServerCA`** with the Let's Encrypt chain and keep `strict`.
126	Scoped to this cluster, but must be redone whenever the issuing CA rotates.
127	
128	**Option A was applied 2026-07-29.** Note the original value was `""` (empty,
129	inheriting `default: strict`), so the exact rollback is `value: ""` — not
130	`"strict"`:
131	
132	```bash
133	kubectl --context rancher patch settings.management.cattle.io agent-tls-mode \
134	  --type=merge -p '{"value":""}'
135	```
136	
137	What happened after the patch: Rancher deleted and recreated the fleet-agent
138	Deployment, the new pod waited out the previous leader lease (~30s), then
139	registered — creating the `fleet-agent` Secret and populating
140	`status.agent.lastSeen`. `c-nnzn9` went to 2/2 bundles ready. Total time about
141	two minutes; **no workload on sdf1 was touched.**
142	
143	One prediction that did **not** hold: the other downstream
144	(`cluster-ee8f7993b3a6`) last checked in 2026-07-17 and was still stuck there
145	afterwards, so its staleness is a separate problem — most likely that host being
146	offline, not TLS mode. Worth a look, but unrelated to this cluster.
147	
148	## ⏭ Phase 2/3 — GitRepos + staged rollout (approve each widen)
149	
150	**One GitRepo per namespace, named `lab-<namespace>`** — see
151	`gitrepos/README.md` for the full table, rollout order, and the manifests
152	themselves. Each namespace can be adopted, rolled back, or paused independently.
153	
154	Order: `lab-node-red` → `lab-emby` / `lab-resilio` → `lab-hermes` → `lab-ai`
155	(eight paths, one at a time) → `lab-metallb-system` /
156	`lab-nvidia-device-plugin` / `lab-cattle-monitoring-system` →
157	`lab-longhorn-system` last.
158	
159	At each step: apply (or add a path), let Fleet render, confirm the
160	BundleDeployment goes Ready, spot-check the workload, proceed. Roll back by
161	removing the path or deleting the GitRepo.
162	
163	Leave `correctDrift` disabled at first. Turning it on makes Fleet revert
164	out-of-band `kubectl edit`s — desirable eventually, but it will fight the
165	hand-tuning habits this cluster has (see the ComfyUI and Ollama notes below).
166	
167	## Watch-outs
168	
169	- **Helm adoption is the real hazard, and `helm get values` will not show it.**
170	  Two releases had drift in the *rendered objects* while their user-supplied
171	  values looked clean, because someone had edited the live object directly:
172	  open-webui's Ollama URLs and Longhorn's replica counts. Always diff
173	  `helm get manifest <release>` against the live cluster — not just values —
174	  before enabling a helm path, and adopt one release at a time:
175	
176	  ```bash
177	  helm -n <ns> get manifest <release> > /tmp/m.yaml
178	  kubectl diff -n <ns> -f /tmp/m.yaml
179	  ```
180	
181	- **Longhorn replica count is the single most dangerous default here.** The chart
182	  defaults to 3 replicas; this one-node cluster runs 1. Adopting Longhorn without
183	  `02-longhorn/values.yaml`'s `persistence.defaultClassReplicaCount: 1` would
184	  leave every new volume permanently Degraded. This is why Longhorn is last in
185	  the table above. Note the *global* default-replica-count is deliberately left
186	  undeclared — see the comment in that values file for why.
187	- **Missing Secrets = stuck bundles.** Create these before enabling the
188	  corresponding path:
189	  | Secret | Namespace | Needed by | Exists? |
190	  |---|---|---|---|
191	  | `github-mcp-token` | `ai` | github-mcp-server | ✅ |
192	  | `harbor-pull` | `ai` | ollama-exporter (Harbor image) | ✅ |
193	  | `hermes-api-key`, `hermes-slack` | `hermes` | hermes-agent | ✅ |
194	  | `hermes-webui` | `hermes` | hermes-webui container | ❌ **create first** |
195	
196	  The earlier note here also listed `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` for open-webui. That was
197	  wrong: the live StatefulSet has no `secretKeyRef` env and no `envFrom`, and no
198	  such Secret exists in `ai`. Nothing to create.
199	- **`hermes-webui` password.** The live Deployment carries
200	  `HERMES_WEBUI_PASSWORD` as a plaintext env value. `10-hermes/hermes.yaml`
201	  reads it from a Secret instead — this repo is public and Fleet renders
202	  manifests into a Bundle on the controller. This is the **only** intentional
203	  divergence between the repo and live state. Seed the Secret with the value
204	  already in the live spec so adoption does not change the credential (keeping it
205	  out of git is the requirement here, not rotating it). Note this is the one
206	  adopted path that **does** restart its pod, since the env moves from an inline
207	  value to a `secretKeyRef`.
208	- **ComfyUI is declared at `replicas: 0`,** matching the cluster — it pins the
209	  same V100 that Ollama holds. Scale it by editing the manifest, not
210	  `kubectl scale`, or Fleet reconciles it back.
211	- **Locally-built images** (`localhost/k8s-docs-indexer:v2`,
212	  `localhost/docs-rag-mcp:v2`) use `imagePullPolicy: Never` and exist only in
213	  the node's containerd. Fleet deploys the manifests; it does not build or
214	  distribute these images.
215	
216	## Verify
217	
218	Controller (this is where bundle state actually lives):
219	
220	```bash
221	# Is the agent even registered? Empty lastSeen = the blocker above.
222	kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get cluster c-nnzn9 \
223	  -o jsonpath='{.status.agent.lastSeen}'
224	
225	kubectl --context rancher -n fleet-default get gitrepo lab-node-red \
226	  -o jsonpath='{.status.display.state}|{.status.display.readyBundleDeployments}'
227	kubectl --context rancher get bundles -A
228	kubectl --context rancher -n cluster-fleet-default-c-nnzn9-eaf6ebdbb298 \
229	  get bundledeployments
230	```
231	
232	A bundle stuck in `WaitApplied` with an empty BundleDeployment status means the
233	agent is not consuming it — check agent registration before debugging the bundle:
234	
235	```bash
236	kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system logs deploy/fleet-agent --tail=20
237	```
238	
239	The old note said to run `kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get bundledeployments`
240	**downstream** — that fails here (`the server doesn't have a resource type
241	"bundledeployments"`), because this Fleet version keeps BundleDeployments on the
242	controller in the per-cluster namespace shown above.
243	
244	## Controller cleanup
245	
246	`2026-07-29` — deleted the Fleet cluster `cluster-ee8f7993b3a6`. It was a
247	**self-registered** Fleet cluster (label `fleet.cattle.io/created-by-agent-pod`),
248	not Rancher-managed: `clusters.management.cattle.io` only ever listed `c-nnzn9`
249	(sdf1) and `local`. Its agent last checked in 2026-07-17 and did not recover after
250	the `agent-tls-mode` fix, so the host is presumed gone.
251	
252	Its cluster namespace held nothing but its own fleet-agent BundleDeployment and a
253	registration ServiceAccount/token; deleting the Cluster cascaded both away and the
254	namespace terminated cleanly. No leftover clusterregistrations — the only ones
255	remaining belong to `c-nnzn9`. sdf1 and `lab-node-red` were unaffected (verified:
256	same node-red pod UID, 0 restarts, bundle still 1/1).
257	
258	If that host ever comes back online its agent will re-register and reappear as a
259	new self-registered cluster. To prevent that, uninstall fleet-agent from the host
260	itself — deleting the Cluster object here does not touch it.
261	
262	## Adoption log
263	
264	`2026-07-29` — **`lab-emby`, `lab-resilio`, `lab-hermes` adopted.** All four
265	namespaces now Fleet-managed; every BundleDeployment reports
266	`ready=true, nonModified=true`.
267	
268	`lab-emby` and `lab-resilio` were clean no-ops on the same evidence as node-red
269	below: identical pod UIDs and startTimes, restart counts unchanged (emby 2,
270	resilio 13), rollout revisions unchanged, no new ReplicaSets, `kubectl diff`
271	clean. Only `metadata.generation` moved (4→5 and 2→3).
272	
273	### `lab-hermes` needed a manual step first — read this before adopting anything else
274	
275	Adoption failed outright at first, with Fleet stuck in `ErrApplied`:
276	
277	```

285	strategic-merge patch laid `valueFrom` *on top of* the live `value` instead of

293	`kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` containing the inline value,
294	which gives `apply` the third input it needs for a proper 3-way merge:

306	revision 13, and `kubectl diff` finally clean: the repo's one intentional

310	live object but not in the repo, when the field is inside a list merged by key and
311	the object is not yet Helm-owned. Any such divergence must be pre-applied by hand.

## Adoption log

`2026-07-29` — **`lab-ai`: the five raw-manifest paths adopted. All no-ops.**
`08-indexer`, `09-mcp`, `07-comfyui`, `06-milvus/attu`,
`04-ollama/ollama-exporter` — added one at a time, each reaching

the three pre-existing chart releases.

**The three Helm paths (`04-ollama`, `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`) are
deliberately NOT yet added** — pre-flight says they should be no-ops too (see
below), but they were left for a separate approved step.

Evidence, whole-namespace snapshot before vs after all five:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Pod UIDs / startTimes / restart counts | **all identical** — nothing restarted |
| ReplicaSets (46 of them) | **identical**, no new ones, same replica counts |
| CronJob `generation` | **unchanged** (5 / 2 / 2) |
| Deployment `generation` | +1 on each of the 8 adopted — inert, as with node-red |
| StatefulSets (`open-webui`, `milvus-etcd`) | untouched — not in these bundles |
| `ollama-exporter` 9401 proxy | live-probed, returns `{"version":"0.32.0"}` |
| ComfyUI | still `replicas: 0`, not scaled up |
| `attu` Service | still `ClusterIP`, Ingress intact |

Note the generation bump lands on Deployments but **not** on CronJobs, which
narrows the earlier node-red observation: Helm rewrites the Deployment spec to
identical values, and CronJobs come out untouched entirely.

The watch-out below says to diff `helm get manifest <release>` against live. That
catches out-of-band edits, but it does **not** answer the question that matters:
*what will Fleet apply?* Render the chart the way Fleet will — pinned version plus
the repo's own `values.yaml` — and diff **that** against live:

```bash
helm template <release> <repo>/<chart> --version <pinned> -n ai \
  -f <dir>/values.yaml --no-hooks > /tmp/render.yaml
kubectl diff -n ai -f /tmp/render.yaml
```

- `helm get manifest open-webui` vs live → **shows a diff**: the recorded release
  still says `ollama:11434` for `OLLAMA_BASE_URLS` / `RAG_OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, while
  live was hand-edited to `ollama-exporter:9401`.
- `helm template` with `05-open-webui/values.yaml` vs live → **clean**, because
  the repo's values were already corrected to 9401.

So the alarming diff is *recorded-release* drift, not repo drift, and adoption
will close it rather than change the cluster. Reading only the first check would
have stalled this path for no reason. All three charts render clean against live:
`04-ollama` (release at revision 14), `05-open-webui`, `06-milvus`.

Two gotchas when running these diffs:

- **`kubectl diff -R -f <dir>` fails on the bundle's own `fleet.yaml`** —

  `find <dir> -name '*.yaml' -not -name 'fleet.yaml'`.

  create it. Pass `--no-hooks` so it does not show up as a phantom addition.

## The rule: one unadopted path per file

**A file in this dir must never contain more than one path that is not yet
adopted.** Otherwise `kubectl apply -f` widens the GitRepo by every unadopted path
at once, which is precisely what the one-at-a-time rule exists to prevent. Keeping
this invariant means applying any file here is always a single adoption step, and
always idempotent once adopted.

`lab-metallb-system.yaml` and `lab-nvidia-device-plugin.yaml` used to carry two
paths each and were trimmed to their safe first path on 2026-07-29. The second
path is documented as a patch command in each file's own header comment. Add it
only after the first is verified Ready. Every other file is single-path.

`lab-ai` is the one namespace with no file at all: it has *five* adopted paths and
three pending, and a file listing only one unadopted path would misrepresent the
five that are live. Commands above.

### `03-gpu/runtimeclass` is not just a staging question

While trimming `lab-nvidia-device-plugin.yaml` it turned out the `nvidia` and
`nvidia-experimental` RuntimeClasses are **owned by k3s**, not by this repo:

    objectset.rio.cattle.io/owner-gvk:  k3s.cattle.io/v1, Kind=Addon
    objectset.rio.cattle.io/owner-name: runtimes

They ship with k3s's bundled `runtimes` Addon and are as old as the cluster.
Adopting that path points Fleet and k3s's addon controller at the same
cluster-scoped objects; if they fight, GPU scheduling breaks for ollama, comfyui
and dcgm-exporter simultaneously. `03-gpu/runtimeclass/nvidia-runtimeclass.yaml`
also carries the `objectset.rio.cattle.io/*` annotations committed verbatim — a
symptom of the same thing.

**This is unresolved.** Decide whether the path belongs in Fleet at all before
adding it — leaving the RuntimeClasses to k3s is a legitimate answer, in which
case drop the path and note it alongside Traefik as k3s-bundled and not
Fleet-managed. It also reverses the stage order the old comment implied: the
device plugin chart is the safe first step, not the RuntimeClass.

Committed as `26a4af5` on branch `fleet-adopt-lab-ai-raw`, tree clean. Not pushed — say the word if you want that or a PR.

## The two files

Rather than delete them, I trimmed each to its **safe first path** and documented the second as a patch command in the file's own header. Unlike `lab-ai` — five adopted paths and three pending, which no single file can honestly represent — a 2-path file *can* be expressed as "path one, then patch," so it keeps its comments and stays applyable.

All eight remaining files now hold exactly one path, validated as parsing with the correct selector, branch, and namespace. That makes the invariant uniform and stateable as a rule: **never more than one unadopted path per file**, so `kubectl apply -f` is always a single adoption step.

## The thing you'll want to decide

Trimming the GPU file surfaced something I don't think was known: **the `nvidia` RuntimeClasses aren't ours.** They carry `owner-gvk: k3s.cattle.io/v1, Kind=Addon` / `owner-name: runtimes` — k3s's bundled `runtimes` addon, as old as the cluster. Adopting `03-gpu/runtimeclass` would aim Fleet and k3s's addon controller at the same cluster-scoped objects; if they fight, GPU scheduling breaks for ollama, comfyui, and dcgm-exporter simultaneously. The committed manifest also has the `objectset.rio.cattle.io/*` annotations pasted in verbatim, which is a symptom of the same confusion.

I removed the path and documented it as unresolved rather than guessing. Leaving those to k3s — same as Traefik — looks like the right answer to me, but it's your call.

It also inverts the old comment's logic: "RuntimeClass must land before any GPU pod" is fresh-install reasoning, and nothing here is fresh. For adoption, the device-plugin chart is the safe first step.

Two other notes: `lab-ai` is still at 5/8 paths on the cluster (Helm paths pre-flighted clean, awaiting your go-ahead), and this session is fairly long — a natural point for `/handoff` if you'd rather resume the Helm adoptions fresh.
